rationale: The specification promises 50/asc; configured fallbacks explicitly select 10/desc. Neither artifact supplies a rationale establishing which defaults were intended.

⚠️ The dedicated refs endpoint retrieves and formats LocationLevelRefs, whose documented purpose is identifiers and effective dates. Its response annotation incorrectly names the full LocationLevels model.

⚠️ The implementation comment explicitly requires provided metadata to override extracted values, but the isEmpty conditions admit empty headers and discard nonempty overrides. The predicates are reversed.
⚠️ The controller promises default true, yet directly parses a nullable query value. Boolean.parseBoolean(null) yields false, so omission changes the advertised existence-protection behavior.

The declared hydra.groups scope differs from the enforced hydra.warden.groups constant. Token validation confirms the discrepancy, but supplied artifacts do not establish which scope name is intended.

⚠️ The contract explicitly supports multiple container specifications and an array response. The structured DOCKERFILE branch directly returns one ToolContainerfile, omitting the required collection wrapper.

⚠️ POST reuses the general Project schema, while a dedicated request struct explicitly decodes and validates project_name. The reused schema appears to describe the response representation instead of the creation payload.
DELETE declares hydra.groups but passes hydra.warden.groups to token validation. Both names are explicit; the available evidence does not identify the intended authorization scope.

⚠️ Non-plain additional descriptors are promised as ToolDescriptor metadata wrappers. The matching-file branch returns SourceFile directly, bypassing the wrapper construction used for primary descriptors.
⚠️ XML formatting deliberately marshals the XMLv1Office wrapper. The XML response annotation points to the CSV formatter class, an evident media-type/schema association error.

⚠️ Version metadata updates accept EditableMetaData, including labels and properties, but construct the storage DTO with only name and description. The other accepted fields are dropped before storage.

⚠️ Header values reach updateArtifactInternal, whose comment requires overrides. Its trim().isEmpty() checks only apply empty values, contradicting both that intent and the documented header semantics.
The OpenAPI default is 2 while the binding default is explicitly 3, and both resource variants are selected by code. No supplied evidence resolves which default was intended.
The group-list contract and runtime guard use different scope names. The guard really forwards hydra.warden.groups, but there is no independent evidence selecting that name over hydra.groups.

The contract consistently names camelCase query parameters; explicit runtime bindings consistently use snake_case. No supplied naming policy or intent evidence determines which interface should change.

The contract explicitly promises a null-filled 200 response, while the service deliberately throws a 404-mapped exception. Both absence semantics are plausible; the artifacts do not resolve the intended choice.
⚠️ Pagination caps the upper limit but never enforces the advertised minimum. Zero survives Math.min and reaches setMaxResults(0); lower-bound validation is missing from the supplied path.
⚠️ Update authorization and storage use metadata.ID copied from the body. The path ImmutableRuleID is ignored, so the identified route resource does not determine which rule is updated.

⚠️ Nested request dates are deliberately parsed from scalar text using dateFormat and locale. The request-only Swagger model instead supplies LocalDate with an array example, misdescribing the accepted representation.
⚠️ The handled-login branch writes the documented 410 object but does not return. Execution then writes the ordinary login request, violating the intended single-response control flow.
⚠️ The declared minimum is one, but only the upper limit is capped. A zero limit reaches the DAO unchanged and becomes setMaxResults(0), indicating missing lower-bound enforcement.

⚠️ The response DTO deliberately models repository ID as int64 and serializes it normally. The isolated string declaration in Repository appears to be an incorrect schema type for that numeric identifier.
⚠️ The code distinguishes incompatible content from unprocessable schemas and explicitly maps the latter to 422. The endpoint response documentation omits this intentional error category.

⚠️ Independent optional bounds require independent predicates. The OR condition makes the entire price restriction true whenever either bound is null, silently discarding a supplied lower or upper filter.
⚠️ The registered LocalDate adapter explicitly preserves array serialization for compatibility. The response-only Swagger date field incorrectly describes that established output as a string.

⚠️ Application-scoped authorization protects the route, but the log lookup receives only ID and timestamp. No application equality check connects the returned log to the selected application in the supplied path.

⚠️ The endpoint deliberately retrieves and formats the dedicated location-kind DTO containing identifiers and kind. The response annotation names the broader Location model instead of that specialized representation.

⚠️ Request processing uses a scalar date and the supplied dateFormat/locale. The Swagger request field's LocalDate array example conflicts with that explicit parsing convention and its own formatting parameters.

⚠️ Schedule assembly intentionally reads repaymentsStartingFromDate through locale/dateFormat scalar parsing. Its request schema uses an array-valued LocalDate example, confusing the wire input with the internal date representation.
⚠️ The handled-logout branch writes 410 but falls through to the normal request writer. A return is missing after the terminal response, producing a second serialization attempt.

⚠️ The contract enumerates permitted sort fields, but the supplied resource/use-case path forwards any field into SortableImpl after removing a descending prefix. No local allowlist check enforces the declared set.

⚠️ Missing products deliberately use the shared NotFoundException and its 404 mapping. The review endpoint documentation groups this resource-absence case under 400 and omits its actual error response.
Member addition declares hydra.groups but enforces hydra.warden.groups. The token guard confirms the mismatch; no supplied intent evidence establishes which scope spelling is authoritative.
Member removal forwards hydra.warden.groups to token validation despite declaring hydra.groups. The available contract and code disagree without establishing the intended scope name.
⚠️ The handled-consent branch writes the 410 response but continues into request normalization and ordinary serialization. The missing return contradicts its terminal handled-request behavior.
Group creation's declared scope and enforced constant differ. The discrepancy is clear, but supplied artifacts provide no basis for choosing hydra.groups or hydra.warden.groups as intended.
⚠️ Business dates use a registered adapter deliberately preserving year/month/day arrays. The response documentation models date as String despite that explicit compatibility-oriented serialization.
⚠️ The API-scoped endpoint passes only log ID and timestamp to a global lookup. Neither retrieval nor subsequent conversion checks that the log belongs to the API selected for authorization.
⚠️ The endpoint invokes the unscoped findEvents overload. A supplied alternative explicitly validates alert reference type and ID, confirming the route omitted the available API ownership check.
⚠️ The public flag has a documented two-value domain, yet the supplied handler only defaults empty values and copies other strings onward. Its local request validator never checks this field.
⚠️ Unprocessable schemas intentionally have a distinct exception and 422 mapping, separate from rule incompatibility's 409. Version-creation documentation fails to include that error outcome.

⚠️ The inherited API explicitly requires a valid non-null expectedHash for assignment. The HTTP parameter documentation does not express that established validation requirement; its requiredness description is incomplete.
⚠️ Even the HTTP interface returns SingleReferenceResponse, matching the implementation's explicit reference wrapper. Its response schema annotation incorrectly names the nested Reference type.

⚠️ The contract specifies omission defaults, but retrieval unconditionally uses requiredInstant for both boundaries. The supplied implementation contains no fallback to the documented 1800/3000 window.

⚠️ The operation retrieves one property and serializes it directly, consistent with its singular description. Its annotation reuses the collection response wrapper, incorrectly describing the single-resource result.

⚠️ Missing status is client-invalid, but data.getStatus().value() runs before checking status. The resulting null dereference bypasses lifecycle validation and falls through the mapper's internal-error fallback.

⚠️ Subjects replacement requires an existing policy entry and always returns the documented update status 204. The contract's additional 201 creation branch misdescribes a collection already present on valid entries.
⚠️ The method description, Java return type, and installed-package service all specify packages. DeviceSnapshots in the response annotation is an unrelated model and should be DevicePackages.
⚠️ assetIds is explicitly optional in both declarations, yet the controller unconditionally calls assetIds.stream(). Omission can dereference null; optional-input handling is missing.

⚠️ Missing device_response triggers requireNotNull rather than the modeled validation-failure path. The local handler recovers typed validation errors but supplies no exception conversion for that IllegalArgumentException.
⚠️ Both the 201 schema and interface return type require a SubmodelElement. The controller creates the element but constructs ResponseEntity with status only, omitting its promised response body.
⚠️ The documented override is blob-id, including a concrete special-character use case. The handler reads the distinct CLOB_ID constant, so the intended override parameter is ignored.

⚠️ The existing-artifact branches lose the supplied name and description before update. Their overload explicitly substitutes null metadata, so header overrides cannot reach the newly created version on those paths.
⚠️ Duplicate creation becomes ErrDuplicateCredentials, which has no HTTP conflict mapping in the supplied code. The admin handler forwards it unchanged despite documenting 409 for identity conflicts.
⚠️ Retrieval and formatting explicitly use RecentValue, carrying a series ID and recent data-quality value. The response annotation names Tsv instead of this dedicated recent-value DTO.
⚠️ The contract declares conflict for existing resources. The supplied backend appends the reference without an existence check, and the controller returns 201, permitting duplicate creation.

⚠️ An unknown server-side commit outcome is expressly documented as 500. The mapper explicitly classifies CommitStateUnknownException as BAD_REQUEST, incorrectly attributing server uncertainty to the client.
⚠️ public-client is explicitly a boolean configuration flag; resource separately supplies the client name. The schema incorrectly calls public-client a string containing that name.

⚠️ Loan data consistently represents interest rates, including annualInterestRate, with decimal precision. The Swagger Integer field unnecessarily restricts a rate that the implementation models as BigDecimal.
⚠️ The model annotation expresses the intended _links name, but the local getter exposes links without a serialization rename. A runtime property annotation is missing from the supplied model.

⚠️ The resource intentionally transforms members into GroupMemberEntity with a scope-to-role-name map and declares that Java return type. The response annotation still names the untransformed MemberEntity schema.

⚠️ The central route registration consistently uses water-user for the water-supply hierarchy and attaches this controller there. Its isolated water-users documentation path appears to be a stale route spelling.
⚠️ Successful Asset Information replacement is explicitly documented as 204 with a void response. The controller performs that update but selects OK, producing 200 instead of the specified status.
⚠️ The upload contract specifies 204 and no result body. After storing the attachment, the implementation explicitly returns OK, contradicting the declared successful-update status.

The contract routes creation under products/rating; the controller explicitly selects rating/product. Both paths plausibly identify the operation, and no supplied evidence establishes the intended public route.

A single-object response annotation conflicts with explicit singleton-list formatting. Both representations are implementable, and supplied evidence does not establish whether the wrapper or the schema should change.

⚠️ The table-commit contract defines unknown server-side commit state as 500. The exception mapper explicitly returns 400 for CommitStateUnknownException, contradicting both the documented status and server-side cause.
⚠️ The contract combines status 204 with a RoleEntity body, although 204 has no response content. The void deletion method matches no-content semantics; the content annotation is erroneous.

⚠️ Per-record failures are intentionally returned within offsets, but their error shape is undocumented. The success schema lacks required fields and permits extras, so these errors are not necessarily schema-invalid; the documentation is incomplete.
⚠️ The contract's own example maps event names directly to booleans, matching the deserialized command. The nested Map declaration adds an unintended object layer and contradicts that example.
⚠️ Permission selection is processed as booleans and passed directly into updatePermission. The Swagger helper's String field misrepresents those boolean switches as text.
⚠️ Both supported converters deliberately preserve absent Kafka values as JSON null. The response schema's non-null string restriction omits that legitimate record representation.

⚠️ Reference deletion explicitly inherits non-null expectedHash validation. The HTTP parameter annotation omits that requiredness, leaving the wire documentation less restrictive than the established API declaration.
⚠️ Merge requires a non-null expected head hash in its inherited API validation. The HTTP documentation omits requiredness for this precondition, producing an incomplete parameter contract.
⚠️ The validator's own allowed set contains averageRating and reviewsCount, matching the contract. Lowercasing input before case-sensitive membership makes both intended values fail validation.
⚠️ JSON-format conversion deliberately parses record bytes into a JSON tree and embeds that value. A string-only response schema excludes the structured values this format is designed to preserve.

⚠️ The existing-artifact fallback drops dryRun and ultimately hardcodes false when creating a version. This defeats the explicit no-changes promise whenever FIND_OR_CREATE_VERSION must create new content.
⚠️ The schema's own example and ISO-639-1 description specify en, matching the parser's en/cy validation. Its ENGLISH/WELSH enum exposes internal names instead of the documented wire codes.
⚠️ The listing documents a designator-mask filter but reads DESIGNATOR instead of DESIGNATOR_MASK. Consequently the advertised query field never supplies the DAO's designator filter.

⚠️ The generic-request endpoint explicitly returns a generic response wrapper with message metadata and payload. DeviceCommandOutput is an unrelated annotation model that does not describe the declared return type.
Rating lookup is explicitly declared at different base paths in the contract and controller. There is no independent route-intent evidence to decide which artifact uses the wrong path.
⚠️ The domain distinguishes numeric value from textual description and updates the value key explicitly. The Swagger request's numeric description field is a misnamed schema property.

⚠️ Transplant's inherited validation explicitly requires expectedHash. Its HTTP parameter documentation omits requiredness for that precondition, so the schema does not fully express the API constraint.

⚠️ The identifier-query branch returns one identity directly, whereas the same list endpoint promises and normally writes an array. The special-case implementation breaks the collection response shape.
⚠️ The method accepts and documents both sorting parameters but never applies them to the event query. Query execution receives predicates and pagination only, so requested ordering is ignored.

⚠️ The parser deliberately treats submitted metadata as the entries map before constructing ExternalMetadata. The generated schema exposes the internal wrapper's metadata member, adding an unintended nesting level.
